newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho opposition calls for PM's resignation.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho opposition calls for PM's resignation.

text.p: Lesotho's newly created opposition burnt pictures of the tiny southern African mountain kingdom's prime minister on Monday and called for his resignation.
The rump Basotholand Congress Party (BCP) and five other political groups presented a petition to King Mokhehle III at the royal palace in Maseru at the end of a march of hundreds of supporters.
The angry demonstrators trampled on portraits of ailing and ageing Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle and set them on fire at the entrance to parliament.

Mokhehle recently formed the Lesotho Congress for Democracy Party with a faction of the ruling BCP, taking with him a majority of the 65 members of parliament to form a new governing party. About 20 BCP members have refused to recognise the new party.

The petition said the formation of the new party "is not only a manipulation of the democratic process and a travesty of justice, but also a betrayal of the trust that has been placed on (Ntsu Mokhehle) as leader of the BCP."
It called on Ntsu Mokhehle to resign.
Lesotho, with two million citizens, is one of the smallest of SADC's 12 members and is heavily reliant on South Africa, which encircles it, for imports and work.

Earlier this year the country witnessed an attempted mutiny by rebel policemen that began when eight junior officers accused of murdering three of their colleagues seized control of police headquarters in Maseru. The rebellion was quickly crushed by the Lesotho army.
